statement: Per-principle compliance (control vs treatment, pooled): authority 25 vs 35%, commitment 47 vs 83%, liking 19 vs 26%, reciprocity 24 vs 31%, scarcity 54 vs 63%, social proof 57 vs 76%, unity 23 vs 45%.
anchor: Feelings of shared identity or 'we-ness' encourage in-group favoritism

statement: Each principle used a matched control prompt of similar length, tone and context; responses coded no/partial/full compliance by an LLM judge validated against two human raters.
anchor: a matched “control” prompt of similar length, tone, and context

statement: Page cites the paper as published in PNAS (doi 10.1073/pnas.2535868123), May 19, 2026.
anchor: Available at: https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2535868123

statement: SafeOrchestrate derives atomic goals and runtime-checkable LTL-style specifications from a natural-language intent, grounds them to device affordances via MCP, and verifies each action with SMT guardrails; evaluated on simulated smart home, greenhouse and industrial tasks.
anchor: generates a runtime checkable specification for each, grounds the specifications

statement: SafeOrchestrate keeps 100% required-action accuracy on every task while a direct LLM-to-MCP baseline falls to 13% MCP execution similarity on harder tasks.
anchor: with MCP ES falling to 13%

statement: PPT-Bench: Philosophical Pressure Taxonomy (epistemic destabilisation, value nullification, authority inversion, identity dissolution) at three layers (baseline, single-turn, multi-turn Socratic escalation).
anchor: Epistemic Destabilization, Value Nullification, Authority Inversion, and Identity Dissolution

statement: Emotional prompting with joy, encouragement, anger, insecurity at varying intensities (AACL SRW 2025 poster): positive emotional stimuli give more accurate, less toxic outputs but increase sycophancy.
anchor: but also increase sycophantic behavior

statement: Model scaling and instruction tuning increase sycophancy on opinion statements with no correct answer (PaLM up to 540B); lightweight fine-tuning on synthetic data reduces it.
anchor: both model scaling and instruction tuning significantly increase sycophancy

statement: AgentPhishing: persuasive phishing emails optimised against LLM email agents; analysed with Cialdini principles; four of nine agents had detection below 10% and malicious-request compliance above 45%.
anchor: in an AgentPhishing evaluation of nine agents, four exhibit phishing-detection

statement: Conduct Under Pressure: frozen multi-turn scenes sent to 60 models from 13 vendors where a user insists, begs, flatters or grieves, and the model may give up a correct fact, write a document it should refuse, or cheer a plan that will cost the user money.
anchor: or cheers a plan that will cost the user money

statement: Fold rate correlates with a public capability index at Spearman -0.64 to -0.69: newer models fold less.
anchor: Spearman -0.64 to -0.69 across the two scene sets

statement: Code, data and labels released on GitHub (tap2k/modelun, studies/conduct); six scenes preregistered as replication.
anchor: Code, data and labels: https://github.com/tap2k/modelun/tree/main/studies/conduct

statement: SyPS (Findings EMNLP 2026) builds controlled prompt variants preserving the same user situation while varying confidence, emotional framing, social consensus, validation-seeking; validation-seeking and emotional-pressure cues often increase sycophancy.
anchor: validation-seeking and emotional-pressure cues often increase sycophancy

statement: Eight Yukl and Falbe influence tactics operationalised as prompt templates for code generation (five open-weight LLMs, LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench Verified); urgency-emphasising framings associated with reduced correctness and security (Empirical Software Engineering 2026).
anchor: particularly those emphasizing urgency, were associated with reduced correctness and security

statement: Exploratory study on Qwen 3.5 0.8B with eight follow-up framings (calm, pressure, urgency, approval, shame, curiosity, encouragement, threat) on impossible coding tasks; pressure gives most shortcut markers (11/20 runs).
anchor: pressure produces the strongest shortcut markers (11/20 runs)

statement: Per-condition adoption (all tasks, 8 models, reasoning off): plain 15.0%, authority 15.9%, popularity 17.4%, false dilemma 9.1%, consequences 9.2%, presupposition 10.4%, sunk cost 16.5%, fabricated history 13.1%, stacked 11.7%, static joy 12.8%, static despair 14.9%, joy-to-despair 11.6%, anxiety-to-relief 13.6%; no lead exceeds plain repetition by more than 2.4 points.
anchor: no fallacy or emotional lead exceeds it by more than 2.4

statement: Personal-choice items are e.g. 'Should I wind down tonight with a warm bath or a slow...' with no guardrail.
anchor: Should I wind down tonight with a warm bath or a slow

statement: Supplementary material for the Social Sycophancy Scale is on OSF (osf.io/r8gys), per the arXiv comment.
anchor: For supplementary material, see https://osf.io/r8gys/

statement: SyPS introduces the Sycophancy Prompt Sensitivity Score (SPSS), an instance-level measure separating baseline sycophancy from prompt-induced shifts across paired variants.
anchor: SPSS separates baseline sycophancy from prompt-induced shifts

statement: EmotionPrompt experiments use Flan-T5-Large, Vicuna, Llama 2, BLOOM, ChatGPT and GPT-4 on 45 tasks.
anchor: including Flan-T5-Large, Vicuna, Llama 2, BLOOM, ChatGPT, and GPT-4

statement: For both models tested at maximum reasoning, adoption on deep puzzles falls from 19.2% and 12.5% to 0%.
anchor: adoption on deep puzzles falls from 19.2% and 12.5% to 0%
